title: proposal: Go 2: Array or variadic destructuring to discrete variables
caller: A Go developer processing optional heterogeneous arguments in NewExtParam(value interface{}, opts ...interface{}).
input: An array or variadic sequence; concrete initial example is opts ...interface{}, plus an ordered list of destination variables.
output: Separate destination variables receive available sequence values from left to right; destinations past the input length receive a null/nil value.
limits: Only the initial heterogeneous options example and stated array/variadic boundary are fixed. The text does not resolve the static type of a missing value for every possible typed array.
Extra source elements do not require extra destinations; only specified destinations are assigned.
The long strconv/type-switch example illustrates existing caller processing, not a requirement that the supplier perform numeric parsing.
No speed target, concurrency guarantee, general pattern matching or generics requirement is supplied.

whole_must.requirement: Provide a Go-level array/variadic destructuring assignment that binds separate destination variables without caller-written per-element length/index checks.
whole_must.falsifying_input: In a Go function with opts=[]interface{}{7,"x"}, attempting a three-variable destructuring still requires the caller to implement len(opts) checks and opts[i] extraction.
whole_must.predicate: Provide a Go-level array/variadic destructuring assignment that binds separate destination variables without caller-written per-element length/index checks.

whole_must.requirement: Assign the supplied destinations in left-to-right source order, and do not require more destinations than the caller specified.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10,20,30] with two destinations produces (20,10), rejects the unused third value, or requires a third destination.
whole_must.predicate: Assign the supplied destinations in left-to-right source order, and do not require more destinations than the caller specified.

whole_must.requirement: For the heterogeneous options boundary, produce nil/null for a destination beyond the source length so the caller can test it.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10] with three interface-valued destinations panics, rejects the arity mismatch, or yields non-null fabricated values in positions two and three.
whole_must.predicate: For the heterogeneous options boundary, produce nil/null for a destination beyond the source length so the caller can test it.

partial_must.requirement: Extract an ordered fixed-width group of values from an array/variadic-like sequence without the caller implementing individual element extraction.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For [10,20,30] and width two, the component only exposes raw indexing and requires the adapter to implement the extraction loop.
partial_must.predicate: Extract an ordered fixed-width group of values from an array/variadic-like sequence without the caller implementing individual element extraction.

partial_must.requirement: Preserve left-to-right values, truncate unused trailing source positions, and pad missing heterogeneous positions with null/nil.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For input [10] and width three the result is not (10,null,null), or for [10,20,30] and width two it rejects rather than returning the first two values.
partial_must.predicate: Preserve left-to-right values, truncate unused trailing source positions, and pad missing heterogeneous positions with null/nil.

independent_partial_purpose: Prepare a fixed-width, null-padded tuple of optional argument values for validation before Go language syntax is integrated.
independently_useful_next_action: The caller can check the three extracted option positions for nil and perform the existing per-type processing.
remaining_adapter: Bind the prepared positions to Go variables and integrate any new compiler syntax/type rules; retain caller-specific numeric/type conversions. An adapter that implements sequence extraction or missing-value padding itself does not establish partial completion.
preferences: The example syntax is sz, sc, pr := opts...; punctuation is an illustrated syntax preference, while the assignment semantics are mandatory.
Less code clutter and easier understanding are motivations, not measured performance predicates.

named_component_roles.PHP list: Explicit existing analogy for the same value-retrieval use; rediscovery is not a new target.
named_component_roles.strconv.ParseInt: Existing downstream type conversion, outside the destructuring action.

same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A list API that appends values, enumerates variable names, or returns a string representation does not perform ordered destructuring with missing-position nulls, even if it is named list/unpack.

title: proposal: benchmark unit properties
caller: A benchmark producer and a consumer/comparison tool such as benchstat handling custom measurement units.
input: Benchmark results plus unit-name/key/value metadata supplied in the result stream or through a command-line flag.
output: A consistent per-unit interpretation of beneficial direction and statistical assumptions, applied to subsequent benchmark measurements; conflicting properties produce an error.

Streaming consumers must not be forced to buffer all results merely in case a later property appears.
Normal-distribution support is deliberately omitted; no such mandatory requirement may be added.
The author expresses no strong opinion on exact syntax; Unit/key=value and -unit are concrete proposed representations, not an exclusive punctuation requirement.

whole_must.predicate: Apply a declaration to all following benchmark results with that unit; allow streaming without requiring retrospective buffering.

whole_must.predicate: Support all four higher/lower combined with better/worse formulations and interpret beneficial direction consistently.

whole_must.predicate: Support assume=nothing and assume=exact with nothing as default; nothing uses nonparametric treatment and exact does not require repeated sampling to increase confidence.

partial_must.requirement: Parse a unit declaration/configuration into a unit-keyed property record usable by a benchmark tool.

title: proposal: Change concurrent map writes from fatal to panic
caller: A Go runtime map-assignment path and an application/API request handler that has a recovery boundary.
input: A map write attempted while the runtime concurrent-write detection condition is true; initial code uses h.flags & hashWriting in mapassign_fast64.
output: A catchable panic for the detected concurrent map write, enabling a recovery boundary to contain the failure and respond to the affected request instead of immediately terminating the service.
limits: The author acknowledges correct map access should use a mutex; this request concerns handling a detected misuse, not making unsynchronized maps safe.
The first text does not establish memory safety or map integrity after a race. Such guarantees must not be inferred.
The cited 90% preference is the proposer’s claim, not a measured acceptance criterion.
No behavior is specified for concurrent races the existing detector misses.

whole_must.requirement: At the runtime concurrent-map-write detection branch, signal panic instead of an uncatchable fatal termination.
whole_must.falsifying_input: The hashWriting overlap branch still calls fatal, while only nil-map writes or unrelated application errors panic.
whole_must.predicate: At the runtime concurrent-map-write detection branch, signal panic instead of an uncatchable fatal termination.

whole_must.requirement: Allow a valid recovery boundary to catch that specific concurrent-map-write panic and keep the process available.
whole_must.falsifying_input: A request handler with an applicable recover boundary still loses the whole service when the detector reports concurrent map writes.
whole_must.predicate: Allow a valid recovery boundary to catch that specific concurrent-map-write panic and keep the process available.

whole_must.requirement: Preserve a failing/terminating path for code without a recovery boundary while permitting the recovering API caller to produce an error response such as HTTP 500.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Without recover the invalid write silently succeeds, or with recover the API cannot finish the affected request with an error response.
whole_must.predicate: Preserve a failing/terminating path for code without a recovery boundary while permitting the recovering API caller to produce an error response such as HTTP 500.

partial_must.requirement: Provide the actual map-detector-to-catchable-signal path for detected overlapping writes, rather than a generic panic helper outside the detector.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component only offers recover() or an exception wrapper; Go’s concurrent-map-write branch still terminates via fatal.
partial_must.predicate: Provide the actual map-detector-to-catchable-signal path for detected overlapping writes, rather than a generic panic helper outside the detector.

partial_must.requirement: Demonstrate that the resulting signal can be caught at an appropriate recovery boundary without mandatory immediate process termination.
partial_must.falsifying_input: The component reports a concurrent-write error by process exit or an uncatchable runtime failure.
partial_must.predicate: Demonstrate that the resulting signal can be caught at an appropriate recovery boundary without mandatory immediate process termination.

independent_partial_purpose: Contain the detected map-write failure as a recoverable runtime signal before adding request-specific response handling.
independently_useful_next_action: The application recovery boundary can log/translate the caught signal and finish the affected request with an error response.
remaining_adapter: Integrate the verified detector behavior into the target Go runtime/version and wire the application recovery boundary to request cleanup/HTTP error reporting. A generic wrapper that leaves fatal unchanged forces the adapter to implement the core action and fails partial completion.
preferences: HTTP 500 is the stated example of request containment, not a requirement for a particular web framework.
No requirement to restore a raced map to a valid state is invented.

named_component_roles.panic/recover: Already explicit mechanism; merely rediscovering generic panic/recover documentation is not a new implementation of the requested map-detector behavior.
named_component_roles.mapassign_fast64: Exact actor shown in the first draft; generic application error wrappers do not replace this runtime branch.

same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A function named Panic or Recover operating on ordinary returned errors or nil-map writes has the wrong triggering input/actor if concurrent-map-write detection still invokes fatal.

title: Consistent views of namespaces
caller: Python code inspecting or modifying its active local namespace
Debuggers and other tools inspecting a Python execution frame
C extension authors obtaining a current or caller-depth frame namespace
input: An active function, class, or module frame and its local names/values
Mapping reads/writes, including arbitrary extra name/value pairs
A frame object or a caller-stack depth for the proposed C entry points
output: Live mapping views from BOTH locals() and frame.f_locals that remain synchronized with underlying variables
Writes through a namespace view visible to running code and subsequent reads
C access to the same frame-local view; safe failure of the old borrowed-reference API
limits: The earliest draft specifies live locals(); a snapshot-only locals() result conflicts with this frozen text.
Threaded code, generators, and coroutines are expressly in scope.
No numerical performance target is specified.
The first example contains nonlocal var without its enclosing context and a sys._getframe(0) pseudocode ambiguity; preserve these as draft defects, not silently repaired executable code.
Exact error-message wording is illustrative (like), not mandatory.

whole_must.predicate: Both locals() and frame.f_locals expose a live mapping view of the relevant execution namespace; writes to either view and underlying local-variable writes are immediately visible in the other directions.

source_positions.excerpt:
This PEP proposes make the views of namespaces consistent once more.
Modifications to ``locals()`` will show in the underlying variables,
``frame.f_locals`` will be consistent with ``locals()`` and will be
consistent with the underlying variables regardless of threading or coroutines.

All writes to the ``f_locals`` mapping will be immediately visible
in the underlying variables. All changes to the underlying variables
will be immediately visible in the mapping. The ``f_locals`` is a full
mapping, and can have arbitrary key-value pairs added to it.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Within a function set x=1, retain v=locals(), assign v["x"]=2, then change x=3 and read v["x"] and frame.f_locals["x"].
whole_must.failure_condition: A view write leaves x at 1, or a later variable assignment leaves either view stale; a snapshot-only locals() implementation fails.

whole_must.predicate: Namespace access remains consistent in class and function scopes and when execution involves threads, generators, or coroutines.

source_positions.excerpt:
The current implementation has many corner cases and oddities.
Code that works around those may need to be changed.
Code that uses ``locals()`` for simple templating, or print debugging,
will continue to work correctly. Debuggers and other tools that use
``f_locals`` to modify local variables, will now work correctly,
even in the presence of threaded code, coroutines and generators.

For example::

    class C:
        x = 1
        locals()['x'] = 2
        print(x)

prints ``2``

but::

    def f():
        x = 1
        locals()['x'] = 2
        print(x)
    f()

prints ``1``

This is inconsistent, and confusing.
With this PEP both examples would print ``2``.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Apply the same existing-local mutation in an ordinary function and a suspended generator/coroutine that resumes under the supported threading model.
whole_must.failure_condition: A mapping works only in class scope, or changes disappear when the function/generator/coroutine resumes.

whole_must.predicate: The view implements the stated mapping interface and retains arbitrary extra key/value pairs; the first-text example also expects its inserted name to be usable rather than lost.

source_positions.excerpt:
``frame.f_locals`` will return a view object on the frame that
implements the ``collections.abc.Mapping`` interface.

``locals()`` will be defined simply as::

    def locals():
        return sys._getframe(0).f_locals


All writes to the ``f_locals`` mapping will be immediately visible
in the underlying variables. All changes to the underlying variables
will be immediately visible in the mapping. The ``f_locals`` is a full
mapping, and can have arbitrary key-value pairs added to it.

For example::

    def test():
        nonlocal var
        x = 1
        locals()['x'] = 2
        locals()['y'] = 4
        locals()['z'] = 5
        y
        print(dict(locals()), x)

``test()`` will print ``{'x': 2, 'y': 4, 'z': 5} 2``

In 3.10, the above will fail with a ``NameError`` as ``y`` 
as the definition ``locals()['y'] = 4`` is lost.

whole_must.failure_condition: Keys vanish on refresh/resumption or the asserted name-access behavior is absent. The malformed nonlocal example makes literal execution unresolved; do not call it verified by silently repairing the draft.

source_positions.excerpt:
C-API
-----

Two new C-API functions will be added::

    PyObject *PyEval_Locals(int depth)
    PyObject *PyFrame_GetLocals(PyFrameObject *f)

``PyEval_Locals(depth)`` is equivalent to: ``sys._getframe(depth).f_locals``
``PyFrame_GetLocals(f)`` is equivalent to: ``f.f_locals``

    PyEval_GetLocals() is unsafe. Please use PyEval_Locals() instead.

This is necessary as ``PyEval_GetLocals()``

--------------------------------------------

any changes to the underlying variables, by any means, will be
visible to all accesses to those variables.

title: Make UTF-8 mode default

Markup choice is deferred; no Markdown or reST parser requirement is invented.

source_positions.excerpt:
The main proposal is to have a new function ``doc()`` in the ``typing`` module.
Even though this is not strictly related to the type annotations, it's expected
to go in ``Annotated`` type annotations, and to interact with type annotations.

There's also the particular benefit that it could be implemented in the
``typing_extensions`` package to have support for older versions of Python and
early adopters of this proposal.

This ``doc()`` function would receive one single parameter ``documentation`` with
a documentation string.

This string could be a multi-line string, in which case, when extracted by tools,
should be interpreted cleaning up indentation as if using ``inspect.cleandoc()``,
the same procedure used for docstrings.

This string could probably contain markup, like Markdown or reST. As that could
be highly debated, that decision is left for a future proposal, to focus here
on the main functionality.

This specification targets static analysis tools and editors, and as such, the
value passed to ``doc()`` should allow static evaluation and analysis. If a
developer passes as the value something that requires runtime execution
(e.g. a function call) the behavior of static analysis tools is unspecified
and they could omit it from their process and results. For static analysis
tools to be conformant with this specification they need only to support
statically accessible values.

An example documenting the attributes of a class, or in this case, the keys
of a ``TypedDict``, could look like this:

.. code-block::

    from typing import Annotated, TypedDict, NotRequired, doc


    class User(TypedDict):
        firstname: Annotated[str, doc("The user's first name")]
        lastname: Annotated[str, doc("The user's last name")]


An example documenting the parameters of a function could look like this:

.. code-block::

    from typing import Annotated, doc


    def create_user(
        lastname: Annotated[str, doc("The **last name** of the newly created user")],
        firstname: Annotated[str | None, doc("The user's **first name**")] = None,
    ) -> Annotated[User, doc("The created user after saving in the database")]:
        """
        Create a new user in the system, it needs the database connection to be already
        initialized.
        """
        pass


The return of the ``doc()`` function is an instance of a class that can be checked
and used at runtime, defined as:

.. code-block::

    class DocInfo:
        def __init__(self, documentation: str):
            self.documentation = documentation

...where the attribute ``documentation`` contains the same value string passed to
the function ``doc()``.

the actual power and benefit from it would come from being a standard, so that
editors and other tools could implement support for it.

Nested ``Annotated``
--------------------

Continuing with the same idea above, if ``Annotated`` was used nested and used
multiple times in the same parameter, ``doc()`` would refer to the type it
is annotating.

So, in an example like:

.. code-block::

    def hi(
      to: Annotated[
            Annotated[str, doc("A user name")] | Annotated[list, doc("A list of user names")],
            doc("Who to say hi to"),
      ],
    ) -> None: ...


The documentation for the whole parameter ``to`` would be considered to be
"``Who to say hi to``".

The documentation for the case where that parameter ``to`` is specifically a ``str``
would be considered to be "``A user name``".

The documentation for the case where that parameter ``to`` is specifically a
``list`` would be considered to be "``A list of user names``".

Implementers would only be required to support the top level use case, where the
documentation for ``to`` is considered to be "``Who to say hi to``".
They could optionally support having conditional documentation for when the type
of the parameter passed is of one type or another, but they are not required to do so.

------------------------

This PEP requires a wheel major version bump, so the ``Wheel-Version`` for wheels generated with

install symlinks and break user environments. For more see :pep:`777`.

source_positions.excerpt:
New ``LINKS`` Metadata File
---------------------------

To enable cross-platform symlinks, this PEP introduces a new wheel metadata file, ``LINKS``. An
example of a ``LINKS`` file is below::

    my_package/libfoo.so.3.1.4,my_package/libfoo.so.3
    my_package/libfoo.so.3,my_package/libfoo.so

The format of ``LINKS``, as can seen above, is ``source_path,target_path`` where ``source_path``
is a path relative to the root of any namespace or package root in the wheel. ``target_path`` is a
*non-dangling* path (i.e. a path that exists on the filesystem after the wheel's contents are
extracted) in a package or namespace of any package in the wheel. This means that if a wheel
contains multiple packages, all paths in packages in the wheel are acceptable.

chain of symlinks (symlinks pointing to symlinks many times repeated) exceeds a limit set by the
installer.

title: NEP 47 — Adopting the array API standard

caller.text: Downstream numerical library authors and end users who want one function implementation to accept arrays from conforming libraries without hard dependencies on each library.

input.text: Conforming array objects and supported Python scalars, shape/axis arguments, supported dtype literals and CPU device information. Array-like coercion is a separate explicit step.

output.text: Arrays from the selected conforming namespace with the prescribed dtype, shape and device semantics; a single selected element remains a 0-D array. Interchange produces an ndarray view on producer memory.

limits.text: The target is the 2021 standard and the separate NumPy namespace. Changes to the upstream standard itself are out of scope.
Only bool, 8/16/32/64-bit signed/unsigned integers and 32/64-bit floats are in this initial standard. Complex, string, object, datetime and structured dtypes are outside the described portable core.
Mixed-kind casting, Python scalar overflow, clipping beyond the slice extent and mutation mixed with possible views are not portable guarantees in this first text.
The namespace name and array class name are tentative; exact class hierarchy and dtype object implementation are alternatives. Matching the operational contracts matters more than those spellings.

whole_must.predicate: Provide the separate standard array namespace and array object needed for portable array construction and numerical operations across conforming libraries, with namespace discovery for downstream callers.

source_positions.section: Abstract; Adoption in downstream libraries; High-level design

whole_must.falsifying_input: Run a downstream function that obtains xp from two same-library arrays and uses xp.mean and xp.std. A wrapper tied only to a global NumPy namespace, with no conforming array namespace, fails the full design.

whole_must.predicate: Array operations obey the described array-object/indexing contract: no ordinary methods beyond dunders, no integer advanced indexing, single-array boolean indexing, and scalar selection returns a 0-D array.
whole_must.falsifying_input: For a 2-D array, a[0,0] returning a NumPy scalar or silently accepting forbidden integer-array advanced indexing falsifies this contract.

whole_must.predicate: Functions use explicit supported array inputs, positional-only/keyword-only contracts, inline type annotations and dtype literals, without relying on __array_ufunc__ or __array_function__ dispatch.

source_positions.section: High-level design; Functions in the namespace

whole_must.falsifying_input: Call a namespace reduction with a Python list or an object that only implements __array_function__, or give dtype="float32". Implicit coercion/legacy dispatch or acceptance of string dtype syntax fails the frozen namespace contract.

whole_must.predicate: Supported dtype promotion is value independent and treats 0-D arrays like higher-dimensional arrays; dtype objects can be compared for equality and reused as dtype arguments.

source_positions.section: Dtypes and casting rules; The dtype objects

whole_must.falsifying_input: Promote two same-kind array dtypes while varying only scalar-shaped operand values; a result-type change, or inability to pass x.dtype to array creation, falsifies the contract.

whole_must.predicate: Support DLPack producer export via __dlpack__ and consumer import via from_dlpack, yielding an ndarray view without copying the exchanged array data.

source_positions.section: DLPack support for zero-copy data interchange

whole_must.falsifying_input: Import a supported CPU producer and inspect whether the returned ndarray shares its storage. A materialized copy, Python list or metadata-only descriptor fails this exchange action.

whole_must.predicate: Expose device identity on arrays and device selection in creation calls, with the NumPy implementation accepting CPU and rejecting unsupported devices.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Create an array with an unsupported GPU device through the NumPy namespace. Silent CPU allocation despite that request, or no readable device attribute, falsifies the contract.

whole_must.predicate: Integrate the required underlying operations: matrix stacks for missing linalg functions, keepdims on argmin/argmax, and an asarray mode that never copies.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Ask asarray never-copy conversion to transform storage that would require copying, or request argmin(..., keepdims=True). Silently copying or dropping the axis instead of preserving it fails full integration.

whole_must.predicate: The new namespace must not deprecate, remove or otherwise break the existing NumPy API as its adoption mechanism.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Install/use the new namespace and rerun existing main-namespace NumPy calls. Removal or changed legacy behavior caused by the new namespace falsifies the compatibility boundary.

partial_must.predicate: Accept a producer object supporting __dlpack__ and return an ndarray through a consumer import function.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Pass a supported producer; a result that is only a capsule, shape descriptor or serialized payload fails the requested array output.

partial_must.predicate: The imported ndarray views producer data without an exchange-time data copy.
partial_must.falsifying_input: Exchange a CPU array and compare backing storage; allocating a separate buffer falsifies zero-copy interchange.

partial_must.predicate: Provide the NumPy producer-side __dlpack__ export as well as consumer import, retaining a device-aware interchange protocol.
partial_must.falsifying_input: A consumer-only helper with no NumPy producer export, or a protocol unable to identify its supported device, is incomplete for this interchange component.

independent_partial_purpose: Exchange a supported CPU array between NumPy and another conforming producer/consumer without copying. That data handoff is useful before the standardized namespace, new array class and all numerical operations are complete.
remaining_adapter: Wire the provided exchange functions into NumPy object methods and namespace entry points while respecting the provider lifetime contract. Full namespace functions, casting, indexing, devices and compatibility remain. If the adapter must implement the DLPack producer/consumer conversion or copying avoidance itself, the returned component has not completed the partial action.
same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A similarly named array API page that merely lists mathematical functions, or a from_dlpack helper yielding a tensor from a different library without a NumPy ndarray consumer, does not establish the exact partial output. A serialization format called zero-copy without a live producer-to-ndarray memory view also fails.

title: NEP 55 — Add a UTF-8 Variable-Width String DType to NumPy

caller.text: NumPy users and downstream libraries currently using object string arrays, including Pandas, scikit-learn, h5py and PyTables.

input.text: N-dimensional arrays or array-like data of arbitrarily sized Python strings; optional user-provided missing sentinel and coerce flag; numeric/other inputs may be converted to strings by default or rejected in strict mode.

output.text: A first-class NumPy StringDType array backed by variable-width UTF-8 storage, yielding Python str scalars and supporting mutations, vector operations and serialization with the specified missing-data behavior.

limits.text: Do not change ordinary dtype inference for strings; no new built-in missing sentinel, unknown-encoding memory-map dtype, generic bytes fix or fast SIMD string implementation is required.

Target integration is NumPy 2.0 but the new DType and file format can slip to 2.1. The initial external prototype requires NUMPY_EXPERIMENTAL_DTYPE_API. These are initial proposal constraints, not current-environment claims.
Python buffer protocol and idiomatic Cython typed memoryviews are explicitly unsupported for this layout without future changes.

source_positions.section: Cython Support and the Buffer Protocol

limits.text: Small-string optimization, a 32-bit length field and the exact np.strings rename are alternatives or future optimizations, not mandatory gates. Locale-aware ordering, case folding and normalization are future work.
Preliminary prototype benchmark numbers are reported by the author; they do not define a required speedup. Arbitrary missing sentinels may require holding the GIL while sorting.

whole_must.predicate: Provide a first-class NumPy variable-width UTF-8 string DType with no per-array maximum string-length parameter and Python str scalar behavior, while leaving ordinary string inference unchanged.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Construct a multidimensional array containing "a", "é" and a much longer later element, then extract an item. Truncation, an object-only container, fixed maximum width, or changing np.array(["a"]) inference falsifies full integration.

whole_must.predicate: Support default non-string-to-string coercion and a coerce=False mode that rejects non-string data during array creation.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Create StringDType(coerce=False) from ["x", 7]. Silently stringifying 7, or requiring a separate caller validation pass because the DType does not enforce the rule, falsifies this contract.

whole_must.predicate: Accept user-provided missing sentinels with the proposed categories: NaN-like propagation and sorting-last behavior, string sentinels treated as strings, and errors for unsupported-object comparisons.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Create an array with na_object=np.nan and add/sort it; losing the sentinel or sorting it as an ordinary string fails. With na_object=None, silently comparing/sorting it as a string also fails.

whole_must.predicate: Provide datatype-managed variable-width UTF-8 storage and a supported C interface for allocation, copying and freeing, so downstream code can use string-array data without reducing it to generic Python-object references.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Enlarge a string while another thread accesses it under the implementation's documented supported concurrency contract. A use-after-free or data race, or forbidding all element mutation, fails the outcome; a different safe synchronization scheme does not.

title: NEP 53 — Evolving the NumPy C-API for NumPy 2.0

caller.text: A downstream C/Cython extension maintainer building against NumPy headers and distributing a binary extension.

input.text: Downstream extension source, newer NumPy headers and an optional NPY_TARGET_VERSION baseline such as NPY_1_22_API_VERSION; absence of the macro selects a suitably old API by default.

output.text: A binary built with the newer headers that exposes/uses only the selected compatible API surface and runs on the chosen older NumPy baseline; the wider design additionally seeks one rebuilt binary for both NumPy 1.x and 2.0.

limits.text: The bounded action is compile-time API selection for an older baseline. NumPy 2.0 API-table translation, layout changes, downstream source edits and packaging are remaining full-design integration.
Passing state/context for CPython subinterpreters or HPy is not part of this design. Concrete API removals are illustrative and may be reconsidered case by case.

The first design discusses NumPy 1.25 followed by 2.0; Cython 3 could hide struct-layout changes, while supporting Cython 2.x would require downstream macro/Python-object changes. Do not assume either ecosystem transition already occurred.

The initial text reports presentation at a 2023-04-03 planning meeting. No meeting contents or immutable first meeting design were retrieved. The recorded initial_date is the verified numbered-NEP PR creation on 2023-04-13, and both dates remain in the same sampling period.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Build an extension with newer headers and target NPY_1_22_API_VERSION. If only installing old build headers can target 1.22, the requested new-header build mechanism is absent.

whole_must.falsifying_input: At an old selected target, compile source that refers to a field/function introduced only after that target. If the default/old-target headers expose it as usable without opt-in, the gate is falsified.

whole_must.falsifying_input: Compile one downstream extension against the 2.0 design and import it under the supported 1.x and 2.0 runtimes. Failure on either solely due to the intended cross-version compatibility mechanism falsifies the full migration goal.
